title: Engineering Platform and Experimental Protocol for Design and Evaluation of a Neurally-controlled Powered Transfemoral Prosthesis
protocol: Use the online testing module to recognize user’s movement intent.
Stream multichannel neuromuscular and mechanical measurements into the online testing module.
Transform measurements into feature vectors.
Feed feature vectors into phase-dependent classifier.
Switch on corresponding sub-classifier based on current phase.
Post-process classification output.
Send post-processed output to intrinsic controller to switch activity modes.
Implement a finite-state machine (FSM) based impedance controller for powered artificial legs.
Generate desired torque output on knee joints.
Adjust joint impedance according to the current state of performing activity.
For locomotion activities, the FSM consists of five states: stance flexion, stance extension, pre-swing, swing flexion, and swing extension.
For static standing, the FSM includes two phases: weight bearing and non-weight bearing.
Trigger transitions between states based on ground reaction force and knee joint position.
Prepare surface EMG signals recording setup using a wireless EMG acquisition system.
Target thigh muscles including rectus femoris (RF), vastus lateralis (VL), vastus medialis (VM), biceps femoris long (BFL), sartorius (SAR), semitendinosus (SEM), and adductor magnus (ADM).
Ask the subject to perform hip flexion/extension, hip adduction/abduction, and attempt to flex/extend the amputated knee joint while standing.
Determine electrode placement locations by muscle palpation and examination of EMG recordings.
Embed electrodes in a newly designed EMG electrode-socket interface for both comfort and reliable contact.
Mount a six-degree-freedom load cell on the prosthetic pylon.
Align X-axis of the load cell with the mediolateral direction of the prosthesis.
Align Y-axis of the load cell with the anteroposterior direction of the prosthesis.
Align Z-axis of the load cell with the superoinferior direction of the prosthesis.
Measure the subject’s weight and height.
Record the gender and age of the subject.
Ask the subject to put on shorts in a private preparation room.
Put a size-fitted fall-arrest harness on the subject.
Attach the fall-arrest harness to the ceiling rail system.
Select seven fully charged wireless EMG sensors.
Turn on the EMG sensors.
Place the EMG sensors into the customized suction socket at prepared locations.
Write down the order number of the sensors and associate them with EMG locations.
Clean the skin of the subject’s residual limb with isopropyl alcohol pads.
Assist the subject in donning the suction socket and verify that the socket is firmly attached to the subject’s residual limb.
Turn on the real-time EMG analog data streaming software.
Ask the subject to perform hip flexion/extension, hip adduction/abduction, and knee flexion/extension and examine EMG signals to verify EMG electrode contact and data transmission.
Instruct the subject to remain in a standing position while holding an assistive walker.
Attach the powered prosthesis to the suction socket with a pyramid adaptor.
Adjust a set of rotation screws on the adaptor until the position of the prosthesis is geometrically aligned with the socket.
Ask the subject to lift the prosthesis off the ground and calibrate the load cell on the prosthetic pylon.
Instruct the subject to practice walking on different terrains (e.g., level-ground, ramp ascent, and ramp descent) when wearing the powered prosthetic leg.
Continue the procedure until the subject feels confident in walking with the powered device and yields consistent gait pattern in each activity performance.
Turn on the powered prosthesis.
Load parameters into the intrinsic controller.
Run a training data collection computer program.
Set the intrinsic control to standing mode by clicking the "Standing" button on the GUI.
Begin data collection by clicking the “Start Recording” button on GUI.
Instruct the subject to stay in standing position for 5 seconds.
Instruct the subject to walk over level ground at his/her self-selected comfortable walking speed.
Click the “Walking” button on the GUI before toe-off of the leading leg.
Set the intrinsic control to level-ground walking mode.
Click the “Ramp Ascent” button on the GUI before toe-off of the prosthetic leg stepping onto the ramp.
Switch the intrinsic control to ramp ascent mode.
Allow the subject to use a hand railing when walking on a ramp.
Click the “Walking” button again before the heel strike of the prosthetic leg stepping onto the level platform at the end of the ramp.
Switch the prosthesis intrinsic control back to level-ground walking mode.
Instruct the subject to stop and remain in standing position at the end of the walking path.
Click the “Standing” button before the double stance phase.
Switch the intrinsic control back to standing mode.
Terminate data collection by clicking “Stop” button.
Label collected data as “training data set 1”.
Repeat the procedure when the subject walks in a reverse route back to the starting location, switching the intrinsic control to ramp descent mode on the down ramp.
Collect ten complete training data sets.
Examine signal quality of collected training data sets.
Allow the subject to rest after data collection session.
Train pattern recognition classifiers in NMI via offline training module using collected EMG and mechanical signals, activity modes, and detected phases.
Save parameters of the classifiers for later online testing session.
Instruct the subject to stand at the starting point of the walking path.
Turn on the powered prosthesis.
Load trained classifier into online testing module.
Load parameters into intrinsic controller.
Instruct the subject to begin the testing trials in a standing position.
Instruct the subject to continuously transition to level-ground walking, ramp walking, and then back to level-ground walking.
Instruct the subject to perform each activity at a comfortable pace.
Allow rest periods between trials to avoid fatigue.
Display the activity modes of the prosthesis on a TV monitor during each trial.
Display knee joint angle readings on a TV monitor during each trial.
Save all measurements and control outputs for later evaluation.
Repeat steps until ten complete testing trials are finished.
